note: Jump rows (pdf 52, 56): J, JE, JD, JSR, JSRE and JSRD share the first word 0000 000 100 and are followed by BB AAAAAA DE and AAAAAAAAAA. Every expect value is read from the cited page images and derived by hand; none comes from this core, an assembler or another implementation. The target takes bits 7-2 of the second word as bits 15-10 and bits 9-0 of the third word as bits 9-0 (pdf 52); JSR forms save PC+3 in register 1BB (C58); DE = 01 sets and DE = 10 clears INTFF (POL-INT-03). No jump timing figure exists, so the bus list is an inference (C36).

vectors.cite: S3.3.5 and Fig 3.3.5, pdf 52; jump table, pdf 56
vectors.derivation: The jump table (pdf 56) prints the six jump forms with the first word 0000 000 100 = $0004, 12 cycles and a blank status change column: J 11AA AAA A00 'Jump to address. Program counter is set to 16 bits of A's.'; JE 11AA AAA A01 'Enable interrupt system'; JD 11AA AAA A10 'Disable interrupt system'; JSR BBAA AAA A00 'Jump and Save Return address (PC+3) in register designated by 1BB', BB not 11; JSRE BBAA AAA A01 and JSRD BBAA AAA A10 also save 'Return (PC+3)' in register 1BB and enable or disable the interrupt system; the third word is AAAA AAA AAA. Fig 3.3.5 and S3.3.5 (pdf 52): three consecutive words; bits 9-8 of the second word are BB, bits 7-2 are A, bits 1-0 are DE ('the interrupt system can be either enabled or disabled by bits 0-1 of the second word'); 'The destination address is formed by using bits 2-7 of the second word as bits 10-15 of the jump address and using bits 0-9 of the third word as bits 0-9 of the jump address'; on subroutine jumps the return address (PC+3; C58: legible on pdf 56) is saved in register 4, 5 or 6, BB plus 4; 'if BB=3, the designated register becomes 7 (the PC) which is the jump instruction', so a plain jump saves nothing. Target $1234 = 0001 0010 0011 0100: bits 15-10 = 000100 go in bits 7-2 of the second word and bits 9-0 = 10 0011 0100 = $234 are the third word. J (BB = 11, DE = 00): second word 11 000100 00 = $310, third word $234. Program at $1000: $0004, $0310, $0234. The PC is loaded with (000100 << 10) | $234 = $1000 | $234 = $1234; BB = 3 designates R7, so R4, R5 and R6 are not written. DE = 00 leaves INTFF (init 1) unchanged. Init S = Z = OV = C = 1 all stay 1. Bus (inference, no jump figure; C36): FETCH at 0 from $1000, READ at 4 of $1001 (word $0310) and READ at 8 of $1002 (word $0234), three 4-cycle word transfers in the 12 printed cycles. 12 cycles (pdf 56). The jump rows have no Not Interruptable note, so prev_interruptible goes 0 -> 1. No status bit changes (blank status change column). Registers and memory not named stay unchanged.
